the households have been able to recover some of their labour force, but that this is not yet enough to return the households to their previous state of well-being, as defined by their livelihoods.

the households of people receiving treatment in Uganda are not necessarily “living better” as a result of treatment.
treatment is not enough to ensure that people living with HIV/AIDS are able to sustain their households and that treatment programmes need to be complemented by other forms of social support.
